A clock and calendar for the workspace bar and the drawer, and (experimental) a drawer that opens from the top or bottom of the screen.
### New in 0.5.0 - **Top and bottom (experimental):** the drawer can open from the top or bottom edge too, handy as an app launcher (Settings → General → Drawer → Side). The always-visible strip follows it as a row of window cards and stacks with the workspace bar when both are on the same edge. Some modes don't fit the wide drawer perfectly yet, so tell us how it works for you. - **Clock and calendar:** an optional clock in the workspace bar (off by default). Click it for a month calendar. Pick how the time and date read, including German "14:32 Uhr", in Settings → General → Clock & Calendar or by right-clicking the clock. - **Calendar in the drawer:** a Calendar mode with the month and week numbers. Calendar events can be shown in both (off by default; asks for Calendars access). Double-click a day or use the button next to the month to open your calendar app. - **Reorder the workspace bar:** drag windows in the bar to put them in your order. With all workspaces shown, drop a window into another workspace's group to move it there. The order is kept across restarts. - **Collapse the workspace numbers:** the arrow next to them shows only workspaces with windows, plus the next free one.
### Install Wimi 0.3.0 and later update themselves: use Check for Updates… in the menu bar, or wait for the daily check. Coming from 0.2.0 or earlier, download `Wimi-0.5.0-8.dmg` below, open it and drag Wimi into Applications (replace the old version). Requires macOS 14 or later. Universal (Apple silicon and Intel), signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

Workspaces arrive (early): nine of them, one key each. Plus a workspace bar, a window strip on every display, and two new backgrounds.
### New in 0.4.0 - **Workspaces (early):** Hyper 1–9 switches between nine workspaces, Hyper ⇧1–9 sends the focused window to one. Windows slide out one side and the new workspace slides in from the other. Each workspace keeps its own windows and its own layout on each display; a new workspace starts with the layout of the one you came from. The window switcher shows the current workspace, and search finds windows in all of them and takes you there. Minimized windows stay with their workspace, and everything survives quitting and reopening Wimi. - **Workspace bar (optional):** a bar at the top or bottom of every display with the workspaces, that display's windows and a layout menu. Turn it on in Settings → Windows, the drawer's Layouts tab or the switches at the bottom of the drawer's Windows tab. Drag a window's icon onto a workspace number, or right-click it, to send it there. Small or Large, its own theme, icons with titles or icons only. The workspace number can also show in the menu bar. - **Strip on every display:** Settings → General → Bar display → All displays gives each display its own always-visible strip with just that display's windows. It's the default when you turn Always visible on. - **Floating apps:** choose apps in Settings → Windows whose windows stay out of layouts. System Settings floats by default. - **New backgrounds:** Midnight (deep indigo glass, always dark) and Liquid Glass (clear Liquid Glass on macOS 26 and later, next to the frosted Glass). Settings → General → Theme.
### Improved - The drawer has a roomier look: corners that match your windows, more padding, a taller search field, bigger search results and clipboard entries shown as cards. - The always-visible strip and workspace bar use much less CPU, so the rest of your Mac stays snappier: windows whose titles keep changing (terminals, progress, loading pages) no longer make Wimi rescan every app. - The emoji picker shows six bigger emoji per row. - The switches at the bottom of the drawer's Windows tab are tidier rows with icons.
### Fixes - The welcome window no longer disappears when macOS reopens Wimi after you grant a permission; it comes back at the step you were on. - Show desktop also clears Finder's windows, and no longer leaves apps without a visible window hidden afterwards. - Unhiding an app no longer brings back windows that a layout had parked out of sight. - A dialog sheet that would hang off the screen (like an open panel on a window in a narrow slot) now fits: Wimi moves the window aside while it's open and puts it back afterwards.
### Install Wimi 0.3.0 and later update themselves: use Check for Updates… in the menu bar, or wait for the daily check. Coming from 0.2.0 or earlier, download `Wimi-0.4.0-7.dmg` below, open it and drag Wimi into Applications (replace the old version). Requires macOS 14 or later. Universal (Apple silicon and Intel), signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

Show desktop now brings back all your windows, and the Hyper key works reliably on external keyboards.
### New in 0.3.1 - The menu bar menu has **Get Launch Discount…** (join the 1.0 launch list for 50% off) and **Send Feedback…**.
### Fixes - **Show desktop** brings back every window you could see (all windows of a split layout), not just the front one; parked and covered windows stay hidden. - The **Hyper key** no longer fails silently on external keyboards when Wimi lacks Input Monitoring access: Wimi asks for it, and Settings shows a warning with a link to grant it.
### Install Wimi 0.3.0 updates itself: use Check for Updates… in the menu bar, or wait for the daily check. Coming from 0.2.0 or earlier, download `Wimi-0.3.1-6.dmg` below, open it and drag Wimi into Applications (replace the old version). Requires macOS 14 or later. Universal (Apple silicon and Intel), signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

Wimi now keeps itself up to date, and gets Show desktop, one-key float / join and a new icon.
### New in 0.3.0 - **Automatic updates:** Wimi checks for new versions once a day and offers to install them. Turn it off or check by hand in Settings → General, or use Check for Updates… in the menu bar. This is the last version you need to install by hand. - **Show desktop:** Hyper D (or the new button in the drawer header) hides every app so you see the desktop. Press it again to bring back the window you were in; the rest stay hidden until you switch to them. - **Float / join with one key:** Hyper F floats the focused window out of its layout, and pressing it again puts it back in. (Replaces the unbound "Pop out window" shortcut.) - **Join all:** a button at the top of the Windows drawer and the window strip puts every window into the layout of its screen, including floating ones. - New app icon and a ribbon menu bar icon.
### Improvements - Layouts mode: pick a layout with the arrow keys.
### Fixes - Buttons in the drawer now show their description when you hover over them.
### Install Download `Wimi-0.3.0-5.dmg` below, open it and drag Wimi into Applications (replace the old version). Requires macOS 14 or later. Universal (Apple silicon and Intel), signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.
